chapter: Piano influences: Teddy Wilson, Tatum and Bud Powell
title: Bud Powell pushes him off the piano at the Crystal Caverns
summary: In 1942 George Treadwell brings a very young Bud Powell, who takes the bench but blames the console piano.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: I guess that's probably wrapped up in the piano learnings in Washington from those people that I mentioned.... During the time that I was down at the Crystal Caverns, when I had the little band with Charlie Rouse and Phil Phillips and Osie Johnson and Tommy Potter and Harry Curtis... This was 1942. We were playing one night. And the shows from the Howard Theatre would always come down after the last show, and have

drinks or have something to eat, or come down just to catch the show and the music. And a lot of times the fellows would come and sit in with us. Once I remember Walter Page coming down and sitting in with us, and some of the other musicians who I don't remember...

But one night, a couple of fellows came in -- they were very young. They came in and listened to the band and everything. We were about halfway through the set, and this guy came over and said, "Hey, man..." He didn't even introduce himself. He said, "Get up and let this cat play. This cat's a genius." And I looked at him. There was this little guy standing over there, he looked like he was about a couple of years younger than I was. I guess I was about 20 then, approaching 21 or something. [IF THIS IS 1942, HE WOULD BE 22 OR 23] He was standing over there... When this guy said that, he just came over and started pushing me off the bench. He says, "Get up, man," you know. So right away, I'm thinking, 'Who the hell is this guy?' He sat down, and I wanted to hear him play... Actually, I wanted to hear what he was going to do if he had that much gall, you know!

Anyway, he sat down and he played one number. And evidently... He sounded good, but there wasn't nothing extra about it. But he got up and he said, "Man, I don't dig the piano." The piano that they had down there was a console -- I

think it was a Cable and Nelson or something. But it was a console piano. And I said something to him to the effect of 'Man, there's nothing wrong with the piano. It must be you.' And they said something back to me and left.

So it just happened that these two guys was George Treadwell, the trumpet player that was formerly married to Sarah Vaughan, and Bud Powell was the kid's name. And I didn't see Bud again until after I got to New York, which I'll talk about later, and we really became friends. But Bud must have been about 16 years old then -- he was very young, as I was saying. The band that he was with... It keeps coming to mind that he was with Tiny Bradshaw's band. But when I got to New York a year or so later, he was with Cootie Williams. So maybe he just came down to do that date with Tiny Bradshaw. Because a lot of times, leaders would put together a band and just come down and do an engagement, and go back to New York and it would break right up.
